paras: The hanging of William Wiggins was the killing of an old man at San Marcial, New Mexico Territory, about September 22, 1882, by men who took him from his house and hanged him over its door. A Socorro correspondent called it 'cold blooded murder' and said Wiggins was killed because he was the main witness in a peonage case. Soon afterward a crowd blamed a local man, P. Carmody, and tried without success to lynch him.

The correspondent described Wiggins as poor, harmless, 'rather shiftless and somewhat weak minded, but not a criminal or desperado.' He placed the killing within what he called a well-known fact, that 'hundreds poor peons' were 'held in abject slavery' in New Mexico and that efforts to free them met fierce opposition. The dispatch does not state the race of Wiggins or of the men who killed him.

On the Friday before September 29, Wiggins was taken from his house at San Marcial and hanged over the door in plain sight of his wife and children. According to the correspondent, his only 'crime' was being the main witness in a peon case, and he was killed 'to save a few from just punishment.'

On a Saturday night after the hanging a number of people concluded that P. Carmody, whom the dispatch called 'a renegade American,' had been 'at the head of the murder.' They tried to lynch him and 'the strikers in his command,' but Carmody had fortified his house and held it through an exchange of a couple of hundred shots. The dispatch closed with 'The end is not yet,' and no report of arrests, an inquest or a trial appears in the coverage.

The only account found is a Socorro dispatch dated September 29 that the Weekly Phoenix Herald printed on October 6, 1882, under the heading 'Murdered.' Its writer condemned the hanging as 'an infamous outrage' worthy of Apaches rather than 'Christians and civilized human beings,' and turned it into an attack on peonage and on men who 'prate about "liberty"' in conventions.

reader.title: Hanging of William Wiggins
chips: Lynching of any race (not in the anti-Black count)
bases: A single dispatch (A2, A3) reports that men took Wiggins from his house and hanged him to silence him as the main witness in a peonage case; no race is stated for him or his killers, so its place among anti-Black episodes is unestablished.

Wiggins was taken from his house and hanged by 'men' acting without authority (A2, A3), but their number is not given and the dispatch attributes the killing to silencing a witness 'to save a few from just punishment' rather than to any claim of justice (A3).
The only account is one Socorro, Sept. 29 dispatch printed across two pieces of the Weekly Phoenix Herald (A2, A3); no other paper's version was found.

accounts.label: Socorro correspondent
accounts.gist: Wiggins was hanged at San Marcial as main witness in a peon case to shield the guilty; Carmody was blamed and besieged, and 'The end is not yet.'

framing.detail: The Herald ran the dispatch under 'Murdered', comparing the killers to Apaches and denouncing New Mexico's peon slavery and its defenders.
